title: Fern stitch
subtitle: Three radiating straight stitches repeated down a line to suggest fronds
excerpt: Fern stitch builds a central stem from three straight stitches that all share a single base point, one going straight down and one angling to each side. Repeated in sequence it reads as a fern frond, seaweed spray, or feathered vein.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), fern stitch entry.

content.text: Fern stitch is built entirely from straight stitches. Three stitches radiate from a single hole at the base of each group: one running straight toward the tip, one angling left, and one angling right. The groups link into a continuous line, with the tip of the central stitch in one group becoming the shared base of the next. No loops or catches are needed.

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Cotton or linen, evenweave or plain

content.text: Lightly mark a centre line on the fabric. Bring the needle up at A, the starting base point, on this line.
Insert the needle at B, directly above A along the centre line at the length you want each frond unit. This is the central straight stitch of the first group.
Bring the needle back up at A. Insert it at C, angling to the upper left at roughly 45 degrees and the same length as AB. Return up at A again.
Insert the needle at D, mirroring C to the upper right. All three stitches (AB, AC, AD) now radiate from A.
Bring the needle up at B to begin the next group. B becomes the new base point. Repeat from step 2, working down the line.

items.symptom: The three stitches do not all meet at one point
items.cause: Each stitch is being started from a slightly different hole near the base.
items.fix: All three stitches in each group must return to exactly the same base hole. Use one hole for all three insertions and re-enter it precisely each time.

items.symptom: The fronds look uneven, with one side longer than the other
items.cause: C and D are not placed at equal angles and distances from A.
items.fix: Mark faint dots for C and D on each side before stitching, keeping them equidistant from the centre line.

items.cause: The spacing between groups is inconsistent, or B is not placed exactly on the centre line.
items.fix: Rule or tack a centre guide line. Step B at a consistent distance each group.
